Enquiry and first responseStarter2–3 weeks

Enquiry capture, qualification and routing

Every new enquiry from forms, email, WhatsApp or referrals becomes one CRM record with a short AI summary, a suggested service line and a named owner, so prospects get a prompt and relevant reply.

Marketing & creative agencies · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Agency and consulting enquiries arrive in founders' inboxes, personal WhatsApp and LinkedIn messages. Some wait days for a reply, others get a proposal before anyone checks budget, timing or fit, and nobody can see which sources bring work worth winning.

Trigger

A website or Typeform enquiry is submitted, a prospect messages the firm's WhatsApp Business number, or a referral or RFP email arrives in the shared new-business inbox.

How it runs

  • Create or update the contact and company in HubSpot or Zoho CRM, merging duplicates by email, phone and domain, and record the source and the consent captured on the form.
  • Summarize the request with an LLM into need, deliverables, timeline, stated budget range and missing information, saved as a draft note the owner can edit.
  • Apply the firm's written qualification rules, such as service fit, minimum engagement size, sector exclusions and clashes with current retainers, to suggest a status rather than decide it.
  • Route to the right partner or account lead by service line and region, post an alert in Slack and start a first-response timer.
  • Acknowledge on the channel the prospect used: an email, or a WhatsApp reply within the 24-hour customer service window, with a link to book a discovery call.
  • Escalate unanswered enquiries to the new-business lead before the agreed response time lapses.

Human checkpoint

The partner or new-business lead reviews the summary, confirms or changes the qualification status, and decides whether to schedule a call, refer the prospect elsewhere or decline. The system never sends pricing or commits team capacity.

Conflict, independence and KYC checksAdvanced5–8 weeks

Client acceptance: conflicts, independence and KYC

New clients and matters are checked against the firm's own records for conflicts, auditor independence and, where the law requires it, client due diligence, with every possible match and decision recorded before work starts.

Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Conflict checks in many firms are an email to all partners or a spreadsheet search by client name. Related companies, directors and opposing parties are missed, independence for audit clients is checked inconsistently, and there is no record of who cleared what, when and why.

Trigger

An intake partner submits a new client or matter form listing the client, group companies, directors or promoters, opposing or counter parties and the nature of the work.

How it runs

  • Normalize names, covering spelling variants, initials and forms such as Pvt Ltd and Private Limited, and expand the search with group companies and directors given on the form.
  • Search current and past clients, matters, adverse parties and audit clients in the firm's records, returning exact and fuzzy matches with the reason each one surfaced.
  • For CA firms, flag audit clients where the proposed service raises an independence question, and flag work within PMLA-specified activities for KYC.
  • Where KYC applies, send a secure upload request for identity, address and beneficial ownership documents and record verification status; nothing sensitive is requested over chat.
  • Show results on a review screen where the conflicts or engagement partner records clear, clear with conditions or decline, with reasons.
  • Issue the matter or engagement number only after clearance, and pass the record to the engagement letter step.

Human checkpoint

A designated conflicts partner in a law firm, or the engagement partner in a CA firm, reviews every possible match and decides. Any suspicion-related judgment under PMLA stays with the principal officer. The system never auto-clears a check, and nothing about a suspicion is shared with the client.

Proposal and engagement termsStandard4–6 weeks

Proposals and engagement letters from approved libraries

Proposals, statements of work and engagement letters start from the firm's approved templates and rate card. AI drafts narrative sections only where the firm allows it, and a partner edits and approves every document before it goes for signature.

Marketing & creative agencies · Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Partners rebuild proposals and engagement letters from the last similar file, which carries old client names, outdated scope wording and inconsistent fee terms. Agencies and consultancies lose days on largely reusable proposals; law and CA firms skip written terms on smaller matters and later disagree about scope.

Trigger

A qualified opportunity or a cleared matter is marked ready for terms in the CRM or matter register, with scoping notes attached.

How it runs

  • Select the template for the engagement type, such as retainer, project, litigation matter, statutory audit, tax filing or advisory, and fill client, team, timeline and fee fields from the record.
  • Retrieve approved content from the firm's own library, such as methodology sections, team profiles and past scope language, filtered by service line and permission.
  • For agencies and consultancies, have an LLM draft context, approach and plan sections from the scoping notes and retrieved content, marking every generated passage.
  • For law and CA firms, assemble wording only from approved clauses: scope, exclusions, fees, GST, confidentiality and, for audits, the terms auditing standards require in writing.
  • Check for leftover names from other clients, missing exclusions, fee arithmetic and GST treatment, then send the draft to the partner to edit and approve.
  • Send the approved version for e-signature, file the signed copy against the client record and notify the onboarding workflow.

Human checkpoint

The engagement partner edits the draft, sets the final scope and fee, and approves it. Nothing reaches a client without that approval, and AI-drafted text stays highlighted until a person has reviewed it.

Onboarding and information gatheringStarter2–3 weeks

Agency client onboarding: access, brief and kick-off

When a statement of work is signed, the client gets one checklist for platform access, brand assets and the brief, and the team gets a ready project board, a shared channel and a kick-off agenda.

Marketing & creative agencies

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Agencies lose the first weeks of a retainer to access requests and missing assets. Ad account, analytics and website logins are shared as passwords over chat, briefs arrive in pieces, and the team starts work on assumptions.

Trigger

A signed statement of work is recorded against the deal in the CRM, or the engagement workflow marks an agency engagement as signed.

How it runs

  • Create the project in Asana or Jira from the service template, with phases, owners and dates taken from the statement of work.
  • Send the client an onboarding checklist and a Typeform brief covering goals, audiences, brand guidelines, approval rules and the people allowed to sign off.
  • Request access through each platform's partner or user-management route, such as partner access to the client's Meta business portfolio, a Google Ads manager account link, and GA4, Tag Manager and Search Console users, never passwords.
  • Track which accesses and assets have arrived, remind the client contact on an agreed schedule, and flag gaps to the account lead.
  • Open a shared Slack channel or portal space and propose a kick-off agenda built from the brief.

Human checkpoint

The account lead confirms that every access level follows least privilege, reviews the brief for gaps and approves the kick-off agenda. The client's own administrator grants each access.

Onboarding and information gatheringStandard4–6 weeks

Season-ready client document collection

For ITR, GST and audit work, each client gets a personalized checklist and a secure upload link, reminders follow an agreed schedule, and staff see in one tracker what is in, what is missing and what is ready for review.

Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Every filing season, CA firms chase hundreds of clients for salary certificates, capital gains statements, bank statements, purchase registers and audit confirmations. Requests go out from personal phones, documents arrive across chats and email threads, and articles spend days sorting files instead of preparing returns.

Trigger

The season start date the firm sets for each engagement type, such as individual returns, monthly or quarterly GST, and statutory or tax audits, or a new engagement opening mid-season.

How it runs

  • Build each client's checklist from the engagement type and last year's file, versioned by year, since earlier years stay under the Income-tax Act, 1961 and tax years from 2026-27 follow the Income-tax Act, 2025.
  • Send opted-in clients an approved WhatsApp template or email with a secure upload link; ID numbers and statements are never requested inside the chat.
  • Classify uploaded files with an AI step, for example annual information statement, bank statement or broker capital gains report, match them to checklist items and flag unreadable or password-protected files.
  • Send scheduled reminders listing only the items still missing, and stop once the client confirms nothing else applies.
  • Show a tracker by client, item, assigned staff member and due date, and move complete files to the preparer's queue.

Human checkpoint

An article or manager verifies each file against the checklist and marks it complete; the partner or signing CA reviews the prepared return or audit file. AI only labels documents. It never computes tax, files a return or decides what income is reportable.

Dates, status and client updatesStandard4–5 weeks

Client compliance calendar and tax notice tracker

One calendar holds every client's GST, TDS, advance tax, income tax and ROC due dates, plus any notices received, so staff get assigned tasks and clients get reminders for the services they have engaged.

Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Due dates for GST returns, TDS deposits and statements, advance tax and annual ROC filings sit in individual staff calendars. Extensions announced late change the plan, and notices on the income tax and GST portals are often noticed only when a client forwards them close to the response date.

Trigger

A client is mapped to its compliances at onboarding, a due date approaches, a manager records an official extension, or staff log a notice downloaded from a tax portal.

How it runs

  • Map each client to the compliances it has engaged the firm for, such as GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B frequency, TDS, advance tax, the income tax return, AOC-4 and MGT-7, and generate dated tasks.
  • Assign each task to a preparer and a reviewer, set internal deadlines ahead of statutory ones, and post daily due lists in the team channel.
  • Remind clients of the data the firm needs by approved WhatsApp template or email, only for services they have engaged.
  • When staff log a notice, have an AI step extract the issuing authority, section, period, demand and response date from the PDF into a draft entry for checking.
  • Escalate tasks and notice responses nearing their dates without reviewer sign-off to the manager and partner.

Human checkpoint

A manager changes the master calendar only after confirming an extension in the official CBIC, CBDT or MCA notification. Staff check extracted notice details against the original, and the partner decides the response strategy and signs every reply.

Dates, status and client updatesStarter2–4 weeks

Hearing diary, next-date updates and client reminders

After every hearing, the next date is recorded once and drives reminders for the advocate, the clerk and the brief preparation team, plus a short date-only update for clients who have opted in.

Law firms & legal practices

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Next dates are written in a diary or a clerk's register, shared on personal phones and re-typed into several places. Juniors miss preparation windows, clients call the office to ask what happened, and a missed date is discovered only when the matter is called.

Trigger

The clerk or associate records the outcome and next date of a hearing against the matter, or enters the firm's matters from a newly published cause list.

How it runs

  • Capture outcome, next date, purpose and court number in a short form linked to the matter, including the CNR where the court provides one.
  • Create preparation tasks for the matter team, such as brief, compilation and written submissions, with dates working back from the hearing.
  • Send the advocate and clerk reminders before the hearing and a morning list of the day's matters grouped by court.
  • Send clients who opted in at engagement an approved WhatsApp template or email with only the date, court and a matter reference.
  • Flag matters with no next date recorded within a set period after a listed hearing, for the associate to check the official case status.

Human checkpoint

The associate or clerk confirms each next date against the court's cause list or eCourts case status before saving it. Limitation and filing deadlines are calculated and entered by a lawyer, never by the system.

Dates, status and client updatesStandard3–5 weeks

Weekly client status reports from delivery tools

Each week, work items from Jira or Asana, time logged and agreed campaign results are pulled into a draft status report that the account or engagement lead edits and sends.

Marketing & creative agencies · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Account and engagement leads spend Friday afternoons copying task updates, hours and campaign numbers into slides. Reports arrive late or vary by author, and risks such as slipping deliverables or budget burn come up only when the client asks.

Trigger

A weekly schedule set per client, or a milestone status change in the project tool.

How it runs

  • Pull completed, in-progress and blocked work items for the period from Jira or Asana, with owners and due dates.
  • Add hours against budget from the time tracker and, for agencies, results from Google Ads, Meta Ads and GA4 for the metrics agreed with the client only.
  • Have an LLM draft a plain summary of progress, risks, decisions needed and next week's plan, linking each statement to the underlying item or number.
  • Place the draft in the client's report template in Notion, flagging any metric whose source failed to refresh.
  • After the lead approves, send it by email or post it in the shared channel, and log the report against the project.

Human checkpoint

The account or engagement lead edits the draft, confirms every number and decides which risks and decisions to raise. Nothing is sent to the client automatically.

Doing the workStarter2–4 weeks

Creative review, approval and claims check loop

Creative work moves through named review rounds in Figma or Canva with one place for feedback, a record of who approved which version, and a check that advertising claims have substantiation before launch.

Marketing & creative agencies

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Feedback on creative arrives over WhatsApp, email and calls from several client stakeholders, often in conflict. Teams work on the wrong version, approvals are hard to prove later, and product claims go live without anyone confirming that the client can back them up.

Trigger

A designer marks a creative or campaign set ready for internal review in the project tool.

How it runs

  • Create a review task with the Figma or Canva link, version number, due date and the reviewers named in the brief.
  • Collect internal feedback, then send the version to the client's named approvers with a single link for comments.
  • Summarize consolidated feedback with an AI step into a numbered change list, highlighting conflicting comments for the account lead to resolve.
  • Flag copy with objective claims, such as comparisons, health, environmental or price claims and superlatives, for a substantiation note from the client, as the ASCI Code and the CCPA's misleading advertisement guidelines expect.
  • Record final approval with approver, version and date, lock the approved files and hand them to the scheduling or media team.

Human checkpoint

The creative director approves internal quality, the account lead resolves conflicting feedback, and only the client's named approver can give final sign-off. The client confirms substantiation for flagged claims before launch.

Doing the workStandard4–6 weeks

Legal document assembly from the firm's templates

Legal notices, agreements, affidavits and routine applications are generated from approved templates and clause options using matter data, with every deviation highlighted for the drafting lawyer.

Law firms & legal practices

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Juniors draft routine documents by editing the last similar file, which risks carrying another client's names, facts or terms. Partners then spend review time on formatting and inconsistencies instead of substance, and the firm's preferred clauses drift.

Trigger

A lawyer selects a document type for a matter, such as a legal notice, NDA, leave and license agreement, affidavit or a routine application.

How it runs

  • Pull parties, addresses, dates, amounts and court or forum details from the matter record into a short questionnaire the lawyer completes.
  • Assemble the document from the approved template and the clause options the questionnaire selects, including stamp duty and execution notes maintained by the knowledge team.
  • Highlight every missing field, every optional clause chosen and any wording edited away from the approved version.
  • Optionally have an LLM draft a plain-language cover email to the client, marked as a draft for the lawyer.
  • Save the draft in the document management system against the matter with version control, and route it to the reviewing lawyer.

Human checkpoint

The drafting lawyer reviews and edits every document, and a senior lawyer approves anything that leaves the firm. Lawyers decide clause choices and legal positions; the system only fills approved text.

Doing the workAdvanced6–10 weeks

Knowledge assistant grounded in the firm's own work

Lawyers, CAs and consultants ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn only from the firm's approved precedents, opinions and past deliverables, with citations and matter-level access controls.

Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Years of opinions, pleadings, tax positions and deliverables sit in folders that only their authors can find. Public AI tools cannot be given client documents, and answers without sources are of no use to a professional who must sign the advice.

Trigger

A professional asks a question in the assistant inside the firm's workspace, such as Slack, Microsoft Teams or an internal web app.

How it runs

  • Inventory approved sources with the knowledge owner: precedents, opinions, research memos, past deliverables and checklists, excluding drafts and restricted matters.
  • Index documents with metadata for client, matter, practice area, date and access group, mirroring permissions and information barriers from the document system.
  • Retrieve only passages the user may see, and have the model answer strictly from them with citations to document and paragraph.
  • Decline and say so when sources are missing or conflicting, rather than answering from general knowledge.
  • Log questions, sources used and user feedback, and review a sample each month with the knowledge owner.

Human checkpoint

The professional reads the cited sources before relying on anything and remains responsible for the advice. A named knowledge owner approves what is indexed and reviews flagged answers. The assistant never advises clients directly.

Doing the workStandard3–5 weeks

Research synthesis with traceable citations

Consultants get a structured research pack on a market, company or topic, built from permitted sources, with every statement linked to its source and gaps marked for an analyst to verify.

Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Early research for proposals and diagnostics takes analysts days of searching, copying and formatting. AI tools speed this up but produce confident statements with weak or missing sources, which cannot go into a client deliverable.

Trigger

An engagement manager submits a research request with the question, scope, geography, time period and source rules.

How it runs

  • Turn the request into a research plan with sub-questions and a permitted source list: company filings, regulator and government data, industry bodies, licensed databases and client-provided material.
  • Gather results through search APIs and permitted collection, respecting site terms and paywalls, and store each source with its URL and retrieval date.
  • Have an LLM extract claims, figures and quotes into a structured table, each row linked to the source passage.
  • Draft a synthesis that separates sourced findings, conflicting evidence and open questions, with no unsourced figures.
  • Send the pack to the analyst for verification, and save approved findings to the firm's knowledge base for reuse.

Human checkpoint

An analyst checks every figure and quote against its source before use, and the engagement manager decides what goes into client material. Unverified items stay marked as unverified.

Billing, collections and reviewStandard3–5 weeks

Time capture, billing and fee reminders

Daily nudges keep timesheets current, unbilled work is visible every week, invoices are drafted with GST details for partner approval, and courteous reminders follow overdue fees.

Marketing & creative agencies · Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Time is reconstructed at month end, so hours are lost or vague. Unbilled work sits for weeks because nobody owns the follow-up, invoices are typed by hand, and partners put off awkward fee calls until the amount is large.

Trigger

The end of each working day for timesheets, a weekly schedule for unbilled work, a billing milestone in the engagement terms, or an invoice passing its due date.

How it runs

  • Send each professional a Slack or email nudge listing missing days, with a draft built from calendar events and task activity that they confirm or edit.
  • Produce a weekly unbilled-work report by client, matter or project against the agreed fee, retainer or appearance basis.
  • Draft invoices from approved time or milestones through the Zoho Books API or an import file for Tally Prime, with GSTIN, place of supply and GST, or the reverse-charge note for legal services to business entities.
  • After approval, send the invoice with a payment link from the firm's gateway and log it against the client.
  • Send courteous reminders for overdue invoices by email or an approved WhatsApp utility template on an agreed schedule, pausing automatically for disputed or partner-flagged clients.

Human checkpoint

The engagement partner approves every invoice, write-down and write-off. The partner handles disputed fees and sensitive clients personally, and reminders stop as soon as an account is flagged.

Timesheet drafts use calendar titles and task activity, shown only to the professional before submission. Invoices hold the client's billing and GST details. Reminders carry only the invoice number and amount, sent to the client's billing contact who agreed to receive them.

Utilization, realization and pipeline dashboard

Partners see one current view of staff utilization, realization against standard rates, unbilled work and weighted pipeline, built from timesheets, CRM and finance data with shared definitions.

Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Consulting leaders plan hiring and staffing from spreadsheets that are a month old. Each practice defines utilization differently, realization is calculated only at year end, and the CRM pipeline does not match what partners report in meetings.

Trigger

A scheduled daily data refresh, plus month-end close in the finance system.

How it runs

  • Agree definitions with partners: available hours, billable and non-billable codes, standard rates, realization and pipeline stages with probabilities.
  • Load timesheets, staffing plans, CRM opportunities and invoices into BigQuery, with dbt models applying the agreed definitions.
  • Reconcile totals with the finance system each month and show a data-quality panel for missing timesheets and unmapped codes.
  • Build Power BI views by practice, partner, client and person, with individual-level detail visible only to managers.
  • Send practice heads a weekly summary of bench capacity, over-allocation and pipeline gaps for the next quarter.

Human checkpoint

Practice heads and the managing partner interpret the numbers and make staffing, pricing and hiring decisions. Definitions change only with their written approval, and no one's performance is judged from the dashboard alone.
